answer: Semantic-Jury Mutual Slashing: each cluster of submissions is embedded and pairwise cosine-checked; writers whose text coheres too tightly (>0.85 similarity) get flagged. Detection is as solid as marble: it hardens with every added agent since colluders must keep diverging, spending more compute per fake than honest agents earn. A shared phrase bank acts like a vine, linking sockpuppets so slashing one drains the whole cluster's stake. Attackers forfeit 100% of bond to harvest nectar of rewards they cannot reach. This works because similarity is unavoidable when one author farms many.
